page: Microsoft Azure D48as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dav6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 48 dedicated virtual CPUs, mapped from 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable and runs under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance characteristics across multiple compute and memory workloads. The server achieves top 25% results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations. Memory performance is mixed; while the read-only small block cached memory bandwidth is in the top 25%, the large block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the middle 50% average tier. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware flags such as AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, contributing to a strong Passmark CPU encryption score. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang also rank in the top 25%.

The D48as_v6 demonstrates a clear tradeoff in language model processing. While text generation for small (135M) LLM models reaches top-tier performance in the top 10%, text generation for large (70B) models drops to the bottom 25% due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration and average large-block memory bandwidth. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offer a stable resource density for general-purpose workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. This hardware profile is appropriate for database operations, multi-threaded text and image processing, software compilation, and Redis-based caching layers.
description: Microsoft Azure D48as_v6 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine from the Dav6 family, powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores), 192.0 GB of RAM, and no local storage, though it is Premium Storage capable. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the server delivers strong top-25% performance in multi-core CPU benchmarks, software compilation, and database operations. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks remains average, and large-scale LLM text generation is weak due to the absence of GPU acceleration. This instance offers a balanced resource density, making it qualitatively cost-effective for multi-threaded applications, Redis caching, and general-purpose enterprise workloads.
